question.text: Theta (time decay) is typically HIGHEST (most negative) for which type of option?

answer.text: Deep ITM options with long time to expiry
ATM options with long time to expiry

explanation.text: The Logic: Theta measures the loss in option value per unit of time, holding other factors constant. Two ideas combine to make ATM options near expiry the most theta-negative: ATM options carry the largest absolute time value (their value is essentially all extrinsic), and time decay is non-linear, accelerating sharply in the final days to expiry. Together this gives the steepest per-day premium erosion for short-dated ATM contracts. The Trap: Deep ITM long-dated options have more intrinsic and less extrinsic value, so theta is smaller. Deep OTM near-expiry options have very little time value left to lose. Long-dated ATM options still decay, but at a slower per-day rate than their near-expiry equivalents. Note: The cited NISM-Series-VIII workbook pages (76, 78, 81) support time-decay and ATM uncertainty, but the explicit ranking "theta is highest/most negative for ATM options near expiry" was not located in the pages checked. The framing above is general options-Greeks theory rather than a direct workbook citation.
